key_insight: A stacking machine-learning model using pre-operative clinical features accurately predicted Mohs cases likely to require 13 or more tissue sections.
clinical_relevance: If validated externally, this tool could help clinicians plan operating time, allocate resources, and counsel patients before Mohs surgery.
method: Analyzed 408 consecutive Mohs procedures with 16 pre-operative clinical variables.
Compared 30 machine-learning algorithms, including ensemble methods, gradient boosting, neural networks, SVMs, and traditional classifiers.
Used 5-fold stratified cross-validation, independent test-set evaluation, and SHAP to identify key predictors.
evidence_signal: The stacking ensemble achieved the best performance with cross-validation AUC 0.891 and test AUC 0.884, with 70.7% of predictions made at high confidence.
watch_item: The model still needs external validation across multicenter cohorts and different practice settings before routine use.
paper_title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting 13 or More Sections in Mohs Micrographic Surgery
